items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Our first night in the Apple, we had dinner with a Swiss friend, named Peter Wydler and his wife Othella. I was their best man when they married in Paris, France in 1949.

ctx.x: When I walked into his room, I saw the reason it had taken him so long to come to the door. His bed was about two feet wider than an army cot and the springs and mattress were about five inches from touching the floor. It must have taken "Big Chief" five minutes to get out of bed and five others to put his bath robe on.

Another day during the week of the festival, "Big Boy" Goodie came to my hotel with some people from Switzerland and introduced me to them. One fellow's name was Peter Wydler and the other was Felix Debrit. "Big Boy" had played in Bern, Switzerland, with Glyn Pacque, the altoman I had worked with in Benny Carter's orchestra 1933 band. Pacque is mentioned in this book back in 37 or 38 and he had been able to stay in Switzerland during the war.

Peter and Felix were jazz fans and Felix advised the owner of a place in Berne called the 'Chikito' as to what jazz men should be engaged or contracted for the place. Felix wanted me to form an orchestra for an engagement in the Chikito, but he had an idea about certain American musicians whom he was in contact with, being in the orchestra. I had no great desire of becoming an orchestra leader, but "Big Boy" was helping Felix push me by telling me how nice it was to work in the Chikito. I told Felix that I would…
